title: SSO session gating, JIT role mapping, and logout propagation
creator: Daniel Park
description: Problem: Our current SSO/SAML handling has inconsistent session behaviors across IdP integrations. JIT provisioning sometimes creates accounts that miss RBAC v2 role assignments, MFA expectations are ambiguous in the UX and not enforced for sensitive operations, logout does not reliably propagate to downstream services, and audit events for JIT, MFA, and logout are incomplete. This ticket defines the spec and implementation plan to provide uniform session gating, deterministic JIT->RBAC mapping, explicit MFA expectation handling, reliable SP-/IdP-initiated logout propagation, and comprehensive audit logging for security telemetry.
acceptance_criteria: JIT provisioning flow assigns RBAC v2 roles deterministically using mapping rules; newly provisioned users have role metadata emitted to audit logs
MFA expectation metadata is surfaced in the session object and enforced for any action marked 'sensitive' by RBAC v2; UI surfaces required re-auth with user-facing messaging
SP-initiated and IdP-initiated logout clear session state and invalidate tokens across hosted and dedicated modes; we have automated e2e tests covering common IdPs (Okta, Azure AD, OneLogin)

Audit logs contain structured events for: SSO login, JIT provision (role assignments), MFA challenge/result, re-auth requests, logout propagation, and session expiry; events follow the logging schema and are searchable in Console
Backward-compatible behavior for older SAML connectors unless explicit compatibility opt-in is applied
No user-visible regressions for non-SSO users; rollout can be toggled per-customer via feature flag

implementation_notes: We will extend the existing session object with fields: 'mfa_required', 'mfa_level', 'provisioned_roles', and 'idp_session_id' (strings) — these are persisted and emitted into audit logs.
JIT mapping will use mapping rules evaluated in the auth pipeline prior to user creation; rules are expressible in the Console and backed by the RBAC v2 role graph service.
Logout propagation will attempt IdP SLO if supported; otherwise we will trigger best-effort token revocation and session invalidation across all serving runtimes.
For hosted API endpoints we will publish a 'reauth' challenge endpoint that returns HTTP 401 with WWW-Authenticate-like header containing 'reauth_reason' and 'mfa_required' to guide SDKs and clients.

Audit events will use the existing event bus and include correlation_id, idp_issuer, idp_user_id, session_id, action, result, and role_snapshot fields. Privacy review performed for role_snapshot content.
Telemetry: add Console dashboard for 'SSO security events' and alerts for sudden spikes in logout failures or JIT errors.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Some IdPs do not support SLO; mitigation: provide clear customer docs and an opt-in secure token revocation fallback
Risk: Mapping rules could assign excessive privileges if misconfigured; mitigation: require explicit admin approval for mappings that grant admin-level roles and add change-review audit event
Risk: Audit logs could contain PII in role_snapshot; mitigation: redact user-sensitive attributes and add privacy gating per-customer policy
notes: Cross-reference: ENG-7421 (SSO session management work from last year) for prior session boundary decisions
